scope: Where the Rust rewrite's structure still differs from the Go owner it ports. Known source-confirmed gaps only, not an exhaustive acceptance claim.

findings.finding: A query, INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE is checked over the visit infos of the build that plans it (`table_privilege::check_plan_privilege`: a query's before it is optimized, a DML's once it is built, a point plan's through `check_fast_plan_privilege`). PREPARE and a new non-prepared plan-cache entry still collect their `VisitInfos` with the visit-only builds `query_visit_info` / `dml_visit_info` (`Session::collect_table_privileges`) and build their plans separately, where Go's `GeneratePlanCacheStmtWithAST` keeps those of its one `PlanBuilder.Build`; and an INSERT's visit infos come from the separate builders of its target, source and values, where Go's `buildInsert` has one `PlanBuilder`

findings.group: DDL: migrate responsibility before deleting implementations
findings.finding: 53 of Go's 86 `ddl.executor` methods (`pkg/ddl/executor.go`) have no counterpart, `DoDDLJob` / `DoDDLJobWrapper` among them: a statement is lowered into this port's own `DdlStatement` (`cluster_ddl.rs` `lower_ddl_with_context`, then a `lower_*` builder) and submitted by `submit_built_job` / `submit_persisted_job_with_retry`; the missing methods include `AlterSchema`, `CreateTableWithInfo` / `BatchCreateTableWithInfo`, `RebaseAutoID`, `ShardRowID`, `ChangeColumn`, `RenameColumn`, `RenameIndex`, `DropView`, `CreatePrimaryKey`, `LockTables`, `CleanupTableLock`, `RepairTable`, `CreateSequence` / `AlterSequence`, the placement-policy, check-constraint, masking-policy, TTL, cache and attribute alters

findings.group: DDL: migrate responsibility before deleting implementations
findings.finding: No ingest (fast-reorg) backfill: it falls back to the transactional merge (`tidb-ddl/src/cluster_ddl/add_index.rs`); with it the status port's `/ingest/*` routes (Go `IngestConcurrencyHandler` over `ingestctrl`'s rate-limit parameters) are absent

findings.group: DDL: migrate responsibility before deleting implementations
findings.finding: Cancellation follows Go's `convertJob2RollbackJob` for every action the worker runs. A columnar (vector, inverted, full-text) index is checked against its table as Go's `createColumnarIndex` does (`add_index.rs` `create_columnar_index`, `checkTableTypeForColumnarIndex`), but on a table with a columnar replica this node builds no `ActionAddColumnarIndex` job: `onCreateColumnarIndex` (TiFlash schema sync, `checkColumnarIndexProcess`) and its `rollingbackAddColumanrIndex` are absent

findings.group: DDL: migrate responsibility before deleting implementations
findings.finding: A multi-schema change has no `promoteProxyKVDiskFullPause`, whose only producer (`autoPauseAddIndexJobOnKVDiskFull`, the DXF add-index task) Rust lacks (D02)

findings.group: DDL: migrate responsibility before deleting implementations
findings.finding: A persisted DDL job step takes its schema from the owner's `InfoCache` at the step's version (Go `jobCtx.infoCache`) with the job's involved schemas reloaded whole from meta (`overlay_job_schemas`: each `DBInfo` and every table in whatever state), and its action handlers look objects up in that catalog, where Go's handlers point-read the job's objects through `jobCtx.metaMut` (`checkSchemaExistAndCancelNotExistJob`, `GetTableInfoAndCancelFaultJob`)

Root HashAgg is Go's `HashAggExec` (`tidb-executor-aggregate/src/agg_hash_executor.rs`: fetcher, partial workers shuffling one mapper per final worker, final workers, `parallelHashAggSpillHelper` spill), and its serial and parallel memory are Go's to the byte for global and pushed-down aggregates (`sum(a)` 12.6 KB, `b, count(a) ... group by b` 13.5 KB, `count(distinct b)` 12.4 KB) (a grouped scan-fed `a, group_concat(b) ... group by a` 14.0 KB and an index-fed `count(distinct a)` 12.3 KB, as a Go statement loop that installs the connection's allocator charges them); its disk tracker exists only where Go's `initForUnparallelExec` / `initForParallelExec` create one (a distinct aggregate's EXPLAIN ANALYZE disk is `N/A`); its fetcher's capacity-0 input chunks fill through the select result's Go `Decoder` (`Decode` appends each buffer once and rounds its rows up to eight; `ReuseIntermChk` swaps a large remainder in), so a four-row VARCHAR-keyed response grows its input chunk by Go's 96 bytes (offsets 5/6) and `b, count(a) ... group by b`'s HashAgg peaks at Go's 13801 bytes; after earlier statements on one connection the workers' chunks receive the same recycled columns Go's do, so the charge follows the connection's history as Go's does (over a server connection the group_concat run after a `count(distinct a)` charges Go's 18.0 KB, the `b, count(a)` after it Go's 16.9 KB; an in-process session matches Go's allocator with an unpooled result chunk, 14.8 KB and 14.2 KB); a cop-side aggregation with no pushed form (`pushed_partial_aggregation` refuses its function kind, or an argument the pushdown catalog cannot lower: X01) runs in this tier on Go's TiDB-tier `HashAggExec` / `StreamAggExec`, where Go always runs it in the coprocessor; in the suites and the corpus only a TiFlash fragment's aggregates (M01) reach it

`IndexLookUpExecutor`'s memory and RU v2 are Go's, on every run: the double read (`IndexRangeSourceExec`, `access_path.rs` `IndexLookUpMemory`) owns a tracker labelled with its plan that each open attaches to the statement's, charged with its index ranges' KV ranges (`buildTableKeyRanges`), the index worker's responses (`LabelForIndexWorker`) and each table task's `executeTask` bytes (`cap(handles)` and the handles, the task's `TableReaderExecutor` at 768 plus its KV ranges and `dagPB.Size()`, the chunks it fills, `task.rows`, a keep-order `indexOrder` and `rowIdx`), the next task releasing the last; each task's reader records `TableReaderExecutor` into the parent's accumulator. EXPLAIN ANALYZE and `tidb_mem_quota_query` match Go for integer, keep-order `_tidb_rowid` and clustered handles (`tests_explain.rs` `an_index_lookup_charges_its_tasks_like_go`). The index worker's fetch chunk (`prepareHandleFetch`, typed by `getRetTpsForIndexReader`), each task reader's chunks (`TryNewCacheChunk`) and a serial projection's child chunk come from the session's allocator, so a task's charge follows the columns earlier statements returned to it, as Go's does (`an_index_lookup_takes_its_chunks_from_the_session_allocator_like_go`: `SELECT b, c FROM t USE INDEX(b) WHERE b > 1` charges 6.83 KB on a connection's first run and 14.1 KB after). A query's EXPLAIN ANALYZE result is written through a chunk taken from the allocator after the analyzed tree opens and before it runs (Go `ExplainExec`), and a pushed partial aggregate's tasks and a root `LimitExec` draw from it too, so a connection's statements reuse each other's columns as Go's do (`pipeline_mysql_client_source.rs` `a_connections_statements_reuse_each_others_chunks_like_go`). Under a pushed index-side Limit the index stream closes once the Limit is exhausted, before the task's reader charges it, as Go's index worker closes its result (`... LIMIT 64` 4.70 KB, `LIMIT 20` 2.47 KB: `an_index_lookup_under_a_pushed_limit_releases_its_index_response_like_go`). Remaining: the fetch chunk leaves out a keep-order merge's `byItems`; a task is exactly one `extractTaskHandles` batch (a whole 32-row response chunk through `ReuseIntermChk`), a table plan's Limit rides each task's request, a local index's partitioned task reads its rows without handles, and the table workers count every task they execute (`an_index_lookup_takes_one_response_chunk_per_task_like_go`); a task's reader takes its chunk before it blocks on the response, as Go's `TryNewCacheChunk` before `Next` does (`SELECT b, c FROM p USE INDEX(b) WHERE b > 90` over two partitions after a plain run charges 12.3 KB, one of the two values Go's racing index and table workers give: 4.45 KB or 12.3 KB, about evenly over eight runs); an unordered partitioned lookup over a local index reads each partition's index remotely, one partition's request at a time, and cuts its tasks at that partition's response chunks (`a_partitioned_index_lookup_reads_each_partitions_index_remotely_like_go`: Go's 4 tasks); a keep-order, global-index or dirty partitioned lookup's index side is still this port's native walk; a global index's unordered lookup reads its index remotely under the logical table, its request ending with `ExtraPhysTblID` and its handles Go's `kv.PartitionHandle`s (`needPartitionHandle`), so its tasks span partitions and are cut at the response chunks (`a_global_index_lookups_task_spans_partitions_like_go`; `a_global_index_lookup_cuts_its_tasks_at_response_chunks_like_go`: Go's 4 tasks at `tidb_index_lookup_size = 2`), and a read narrowed to some partitions sends Go's `in(_tidb_tid, ...)` Selection in its index request (`AddSelectionConditionForGlobalIndex`; `a_narrowed_global_index_lookup_filters_its_entries_in_the_store_like_go`, its index side counting each `idxResult.Next` as Go's does), and a keep-order one reads its index in order the same way (`a_keep_order_global_index_lookup_reads_its_index_remotely_like_go`), each task's one table request returning `ExtraPhysTblID`, by which its keep-order worker matches each row to its partition handle as Go's does; at the default lookup size a plain `SELECT * FROM t USE INDEX(ub) WHERE b > 1` peaks at 19,440 bytes where Go's peaks at 18,960, and its `ORDER BY b` at 50,686 where Go's peaks at 57,614 (its table worker's chunks come from the allocator at 896 and 8,192 bytes), neither yet traced tracker by tracker; a dirty global lookup still walks natively, as does a full read of a table adding or dropping partitions (Go's plan carries the `_tidb_tid` Selection there too, this port's does not), each task is one table reader whose one request spans its partitions (`SetPartitionsAndHandles`), unpaged as Go's lookup table reader is, so its region tasks are store-batched as Go's are (8 cop tasks in 4 RPCs, `store_batch_num: 4`, RU 2.38; the statement 23.3 KB where Go's racing workers give 20.5 to 23.2 KB); a task's table-side partial aggregate is pushed for integer, clustered and partitioned tables alike (`tests_slow_log.rs` `an_index_lookups_partial_aggregate_request_peaks_like_go`: each statement peak Go's to the byte); the index side reads its next handle batch as soon as it hands a task off, as Go's index worker does, so the response it drained is released before the task's reader charges (6 rows at `tidb_index_lookup_size` 2: Go's and this port's one 2.58 KB task, `an_index_lookup_releases_its_drained_index_response_before_the_task_like_go`; `p ... PARTITION BY HASH(a) PARTITIONS 2`, `b > 1`: both two tasks, 5.13 KB); a task the store answers without a table reader (`LookupFetch::LocalFallback`: a dirty transaction's read, a refused remote shape) charges nothing; a `LocalIndexLookUp`'s index-side responses hold handles where Go's hold the completed rows; and the reader is one source shared with `IndexReader` and index-merge partials, its tasks windows of one `LookupPipeline` over a `LanePool`, not Go's index worker, table workers and `resultCh`

`IndexJoin` and `IndexHashJoin` are Go's `IndexLookUpJoin` and `IndexNestedLoopHashJoin` (`join/index_lookup_join.rs`, `join/index_lookup_hash_join.rs`: outer and inner workers over `Joiner`), with Go's task memory and matching; the fused `JoinExec` lookup strategy is gone. Two gaps remain: Go's `IndexLookUpMergeJoin` executor (and `PhysicalIndexMergeJoin`'s `KeyOff2KeyOffOrderByIdx`, `CompareFuncs`, `NeedOuterSort`, `Desc`) is unported -- neither planner builds one on this branch, and the builder refuses the kind; each task's inner reader is built afresh from the lookup's template on the inner worker that runs it, as Go's `BuildExecutorForIndexJoin` builds it (only a lookup publishing shared probes keeps the one shared reader); its inner `IndexLookUp` (`IndexJoinLookupExec`) charges Go's per-task `IndexLookUpExecutor` (its tracker, index worker request, response-chunk tasks and their charges, `an_index_join_charges_its_inner_index_lookup_like_go`) without being one: each task's reader registers its runtime stats when it closes, as Go's `RegisterStats` does (`index_task`, `table_task` and its table readers' loops: `an_index_joins_inner_lookups_register_their_stats_per_task_like_go`), its index worker stops at its stream's end as Go's does (Go's 11 index-plan loops over 7 inner tasks), and each task's reader is its own executor in the plan's basic stats (Go's merged `total_` form) with Go's `next` waits

The embedded store's coprocessor runs every DAG through Go's `mppExec` chain (`tidb-unistore-cophandler` `mpp.rs`, `mpp_exec.rs`), filters condition by condition as Go's `VectorizedFilter` does, and answers errors as `genRespWithMPPExec` does (`SelectResponse.error`, a conflict's `OtherError`, an unsupported executor's `OtherError`), but the index-lookup push-down is absent end to end: a `LocalIndexLookUp` plan (the `index_lookup_pushdown` hint, `tidb_index_lookup_pushdown_policy`) runs as this tier's own double read (`physical_builder.rs` `lower_index_lookup_selections`) where Go's `IndexLookUpExecutor` sends one `IndexLookUp` DAG and reads its rows and `IntermediateOutputs`, and this tier's coprocessor refuses `buildIndexLookUp`

A TiKV reader builds its DAG from its access path's scan request (`cop_reader.rs`; `cop_plan_ids_for` matches executors to the pushed nodes by kind) where Go's `constructDAGReq` lowers the reader's pushed plan one node per executor (`ToPB`). A pushed TopN (a reader's, or an IndexLookUp's index side) reaches the coprocessor through the scan's offer, its `ByItem`s expressions over the scan's output as `PhysicalTopN.ToPB` lowers them, and an IndexLookUp's table-side TopN (`TopN(Probe)`) rides every table task's request, as Go's `buildTableReader` over `tblPlans` sends it (`an_index_lookup_pushes_its_table_side_topn_into_each_task_like_go`). A covering `IndexReader`'s pushed Projection of columns is lowered as the request's Projection executor (over the scan, or over its pushed Selection through `accept_post_filter_projection`), and a covering reader over a pushed Selection returns only its `OutputColumns`, as Go's `dagReq.OutputOffsets`, under a pushed Limit too (the in-reader Limit narrows its source once the Selection is in: `SELECT a FROM t WHERE c > 2 LIMIT 3`'s reader charges Go's 295 Bytes); a covering reader decodes its response straight into its parent's chunk (Go `e.result.Next(ctx, req)`) when the request returns exactly its columns; and a TableReader's pushed Projection that computes (`j->'$.x'`) is the request's last executor too, its computed rows what the response returns (`a_reader_pushes_its_computing_projection_into_the_request_like_go`: Go's 1.96 KB where the scan's whole rows took 24.8 KB); but an index reader's computing Projection still runs as a local executor, and a TableReader's Projection of columns travels as `OutputOffsets` rather than Go's Projection executor

A projection's vectorized result column takes the shape its Go builtin's `vecEval*` gives it (`chunk_executor.rs`: `Resize*`, `Reserve*` and appends, one argument evaluated into it, a column's `CopyReconstruct`) for arithmetic, comparisons and `IN`, logic, `NOT`/`IS NULL`/`IS TRUE`, casts, `IF`/`IFNULL`/`CASE`/`COALESCE`, `GREATEST`/`LEAST` (a string one ping-pongs `result` with two buffers, reserving it before its rows land), the math, time, JSON, info and common string builtins, `ADDTIME`/`SUBTIME`, `CONVERT_TZ`, `ANY_VALUE` and `SETVAR`; a tree holding a builtin outside that table still appends row by row: the less common string, encryption and miscellaneous builtins; a string `GREATEST`/`LEAST` shapes `result` as Go's kernels do (`Evaluator::run`'s `string_extremum_vec`: the direct signature's ping-pong appends a computed first argument's rows, then each even step's running value after a `ReserveString(n)`, and copies an even count's last step in by `CopyConstruct`; the compare-as-time signature evaluates every argument into `result` before its values), and a compare-as-time call is built as Go's is (its signature kept from the uncast arguments, every argument cast to a string, `doTimeConversionForGL`'s truncation and `checkMonthDay` warnings, a `strconv.Atoi` failure raised as 1105). The values still come from the row and batch evaluators rather than Go's `vecEval*` kernels, but under Go's `EvalExpr` choice (`vecEnabled && expr.Vectorized()`, scoped per projected expression and per filter; a Selection reads `tidb_enable_vectorized_expression` as Go's `SelectionExec` does) a string `GREATEST`/`LEAST` answers the later of two equal arguments as `vecEvalString` does, where a folded constant or a row evaluation keeps the earlier (`evalString`); a tree this port's `vectorized` table does not cover still answers the row value, and `IF`'s row fallback when its condition warns (`fallbackEval*`, which resizes) is not modelled

The session's reusable chunk allocator is Go's (`Session::chunk_alloc`, Go `clientConn.chunkAlloc`: installed per statement as `NewSyncAllocator(alloc)` under `tidb_enable_reuse_chunk`, never for an internal `InRestrictedSQL` statement, reset between statements and recreated after a failed one, each statement's validity its own), executors take it as `ExecutorMeta::alloc_pool` (Go `AllocPool`) for `NewChunk` / `TryNewCacheChunk` / `NewChunkWithCapacity`, and Go's `NewFirstChunk` sites (`Executor::new_first_chunk`: projection workers, hash-join probe and result chunks, index-hash-join results, shuffle holders, the drained record set) allocate outside it, so memory charges match Go's in sequence (`a_projection_sizes_its_result_columns_as_go_vec_eval_does`, `explain_analyze_dml_roots_report_their_executor_stats_and_memory_like_go`). The connection writes a result through a chunk from the statement's allocator (`writeChunks`' `rs.NewChunk(GetChunkAllocator())`, `ResultSetSource::new_write_chunk`), and a covering `IndexReader` returns its `OutputColumns` from the source itself (`dagReq.OutputOffsets`) instead of through a projection's pooled chunk, so a later statement reuses the same columns Go's does: a point UPDATE's root charges Go's 638 / 889 Bytes / 1.11 KB over the wire after a point UPDATE, `select 1` or a scan (`pipeline_mysql_client_source.rs` `explain_for_connection_charges_reused_chunks_like_go`). An `INSERT ... SELECT` reads its source into a chunk from the statement's allocator taken once the source is open (Go `insertRowsFromSelect`'s `TryNewCacheChunk(selectExec)`), so the next statement reuses the columns it grew (`an_insert_select_returns_its_source_chunk_to_the_allocator_like_go`). A parallel projection's last answer swaps in the output its fetcher completed empty, and a Projection under a UnionAll copies its columns (`avoidColumnEvaluatorForProjBelowUnion`), as Go's do (`a_parallel_projection_swaps_in_its_last_output_like_go`). Remaining: executors built outside the physical builder's `meta` (`ExecutorMeta::new` in other crates and builder arms) allocate fresh; a materialized result (a plain EXPLAIN, SHOW and the other row-built statements) takes its write chunk from the allocator when its rows are already built (`a_plain_explain_and_a_show_write_through_pooled_chunks_like_go`, against the server binary), so a statement whose Go executor draws from the allocator before `Next` builds its rows (an EXPLAIN ANALYZE of a write, whose `ExplainExec` runs the write in `Next`) takes it after those draws; parallel apply's chunks, whose executor shape differs from Go's, are unmapped.
IMPORT INTO refuses (`tidb-session/src/dispatch.rs`)

A text `EXECUTE` of a cached prepared write runs inside the `EXECUTE`'s one statement lifecycle (`execute_cached_prepared_dml` no longer opens a nested `run_with_columns_using`), so it has one `StatementMemory` tracker, as Go's one `StmtCtx` does. The process plan follows Go's `SetProcessInfo`. A binary-protocol EXECUTE publishes no plan of its own (`runStmt`'s nil `currentPlan`), so the process info keeps the last valid plan, its brief binary plan and its collector. A SET, USE, DDL or transaction-control statement's plan renders no rows under `EXPLAIN FOR CONNECTION`. Both match a Go tidb-server over the wire (`unistore_cop.rs` `explain_for_connection_follows_gos_process_plan`). Remaining: the statement boundary is per attempt, not per statement. `begin_statement_execution` (Go `ResetContextOfStmt`) runs inside each attempt's entry (`open_prepared_point_get`, `open_prepared_record_set_for`, `open_bound_record_set_for`, `run_with_columns_using`) on the text and binary paths, so a lock-conflict or autocommit retry re-begins the statement where Go's `handlePessimisticLockError` (`adapter.go`) and `session.retry` keep its `StmtCtx` and call `ResetForRetry`; and a binary-protocol `EXECUTE` (`cluster_session_node` `execute_general`) binds its cached point, SELECT or DML plan before that boundary, so a plan-cache miss builds its planner context (`statement_context_for_stmt`) under the previous statement's authority. Go's `ExecuteStmt` runs `PrepareTxnCtx` and `ResetContextOfStmt` once, before `Compile`'s plan-cache lookup. No wire-visible symptom found (warnings, `last_plan_from_cache` and bindings match Go over the binary protocol).

`ReportMinStartTS` has no InfoCache recent-schema TS (`GetAndResetRecentInfoSchemaTS`, InfoSchema V2: I04). Lazy cursor fetch answers Go's `executor.Detach` over the physical plan (`tidb_executor::detach`), because the builder's operator tree is not Go's executor tree

No cross-keyspace runtime (null keyspace only); the next-gen-only surfaces built on it have no port either: the status port's `/dxf/*` and `/ddl/check/*`, the DXF framework's metering and `GetScheduleStatus` (`pkg/dxf/framework/metering`, `schstatus`), and plan replayer's `tidb_cloud_storage_uri` storage (`pkg/planner/extstore` `createGlobalExtStorage`, local files on a classic kernel)

An MPP reader runs as Go's `MPPGather` over Go's local coordinator (`tidb-executor` `mpp_gather.rs`, `local_mpp_coordinator.rs`): the planner's fragments (`GenerateRootMPPTasks`), each fragment's `ToPB` DAG dispatched to its tasks, the root tasks' packets received; the embedded store serves Go's MPP tasks, tunnels and exchange/join executors, and Go's `tiflashtest` tests pass on mock TiFlash stores (`TestMppExecution`, `TestReadUnsigedPK`, `TestJoinRace`, `TestInjectExtraProj`, `TestMppEnum`, `TestMppUnionAll`, `TestUnionWithEmptyDualTable`, `TestAvgOverflow`, `TestMppApply`, `TestTiFlashVirtualColumn`, `TestAggPushDownApplyAll`, `TestAggPushDownCountStar`, `TestIssue41014`, `TestMPP47766`, `TestAggPushDownUnionAndMPP`, `TestGroupStreamAggOnTiFlash`, `TestIssue50358`, `TestNonsupportCharsetTable`, `TestIssue57149`, `TestCanGenerateTiFlashCopWithKeepOrer`, `TestIssue59877`, `TestForbidTiFlashIfExtraPhysTableIDIsNeeded`, `TestIndexMergeCarePreferTiflash`, `TestTiFlashPlanCacheable`, and the enforcempp casetest `TestMPPMultiDistinct3Stage`; `unistore_cop/mpp_execution.rs`). Partitioned reads are Go's too (the generator's `partitionPruning`, per-partition task building and `TableRegions`, a union scan's buffer read; `TestReadPartitionTable`, `TestTiflashEmptyDynamicPruneResult`). TiFlash late materialization is Go's (`tiflash_predicate_push_down.rs`: the scan's pushed down filter, its `lm_col_scan` cost and `PushedDownFilterConditions`). Left: a TiFlash scan's `UsedColumnarIndexes` (vector, inverted and full-text indexes, with the inverted-index arm of `handleTiFlashPredicatePushDown`), the disaggregated (consistent-hash) task building for a partitioned request, the MPP CTE operators (CTE sink and source with their `ToPB`, the generator's CTE task counts and `fillLocalCTECounts`), the index scan's `ToPB`, the local index lookup in `ToPB` and the store (`indexLookUpExec`), the dispatch meta's SQL and plan digests, the coordinator's zone helper, and the single-fragment lowering (`mpp_coordinator.rs` `open_mpp_scan`) a non-MPP TiFlash read still takes where Go reads TiFlash through batch-cop or cop (no batch-cop client or `BatchCoprocessor` server here). Go's `tiflashtest` tests not yet run here: `TestCancelMppTasks`, the `TestDisaggregatedTiFlash*` four, `TestDispatchTaskRetry`, `TestIssue59703`, `TestMPPMemoryTracker`, `TestMPPRecovery`, `TestMppAggShouldAlignFinalMode`, `TestMppGoroutinesExitFromErrors`, `TestMppStoreCntWithErrors`, `TestMppTableReaderCacheForSingleSQL`, `TestMppVersionError`, `TestNoAliveTiFlashRetry`, `TestPartitionTable`, `TestTiFlashComputeDispatchPolicy`, the `TestTiFlashPartitionTable*` four, `TestTiflashPartitionTableScan`, `TestTiflashSupportStaleRead` and `TestUnionScan`

`pkg/executor/mppcoordmanager` (`MPPCoordinatorManager`: coordinator registration, `detectAndDelete` expiry, the server address) and the RPC server's `ReportMPPTaskStatus` have no port, so TiFlash's task-status reports reach no coordinator; Go's coordinator only asks TiFlash for reports when its plan has a Limit above the table reader (`needReportExecutionSummary`), which the single-fragment scan never builds (M01)

PD's `serviceDiscovery` (`servicediscovery/service_discovery.go`) is not one owner here: member updates and the leader connection live in `pd/cluster.rs` / `pd/retry.rs`, with no per-member `serviceClient`, no `apiCandidateNodes` / `GetServiceClientByKind` (how Go picks a follower for a follower-handled region API) and no `checkServiceModeChanged`

Go's `doOptimize` takes `CascadesOptimize` (memo exploration and implementation, `pkg/planner/cascades`) when `tidb_enable_cascades_planner` is ON (default OFF, experimental); this port has only `VolcanoOptimize`, so the variable is accepted and changes nothing

SQL/PB signature construction. Go's `functionClass.getFunction` returns one signature object that carries the wrapped arguments, the return type, the `PbCode` and the evaluation. Here every name in Go's `funcs` map has its function class (`builtin::funcs`), `new_function` is the only builder, and the cast, `getvar` (with `convertReadonlyVarToConst`), `values`, `to_binary` / `from_binary` builders are Go's (`BuildCastFunction`, `BuildGetVarFunction`, `NewValuesFunc`, `BuildToBinaryFunction`, `BuildFromBinaryFunction`); the classes are compared with Go's `NewFunction` in `tidb-expr/testdata/function_class_matrix.txt` and `cast_class_matrix.txt`. What is still not one object: the class returns the arguments, the type, the `PbCode` and a few signature fields, and evaluation is found again from the function's name (`scalar_function.rs`, `func::eval_func_values`); `pushdown_catalog.rs` describes a call for the converter again from the name and the argument types (the `PbCode` itself is read from the node); the decoder builds its own evaluators; a collation post-pass (`derive_tree_collation`, `restore_function_result_charset`) runs after the classes; the AES IV signatures are chosen at evaluation where Go binds them at build; `castAsArrayFunctionClass` and the extension function classes are not ported; five callers with no build context pass `UnfoldedBuildContext`; the planner's `BuiltinFunctionUsageInc` (`expressionRewriter.newFunction`) is not called. Go's alternative-plan rounds (`optimize`'s `fts-like-fallback`) are one AST rewrite before planning here (`fts_like_rewrite`): the LIKE plan does not compete with the native one on cost and `FTSFunctionIsUsed` is never set; `MATCH` in an uncorrelated scalar or `EXISTS` subquery or under `DO` takes the fallback where Go raises 1105; a view's body is not rewritten; an `AGAINST` that folds to a constant (`concat(...)`) or reads a user variable (`convertReadonlyVarToConst`) is not the fallback's search string; `match(<non-string column>) against(?)` is refused at EXECUTE where Go refuses it at PREPARE; a prepared fallback execution that fails loses its skip-plan-cache warning; and `fts_match_word` has no starter-deployment form.

Push-down refusal warnings: Go's `canScalarFuncPushDown` appends `Scalar function '...'(signature: ..., return type: ...) is not supported to push down to <store> now.` through the session's `PushDownContext` (statement warnings under EXPLAIN, extra warnings otherwise; `MppWarningSink::append_push_down_warning`) at every `PushDownExprs` / `CanExprsPushDown` call. Reporting now: the DataSource's `kv.UnSpecified` split, the scan-filter splits (`split_scan_filters` for TiKV and TiFlash table scans and index lookups, index merge's `extractFiltersForIndexMerge`), and `task_attach.rs`'s selection, projection and TopN checks (Go's two `EQJson` warnings over an MPP scan, `json_comparison_stays_above_the_mpp_reader_as_go`). `CheckAggCanPushCop` and `checkCanPushDownToMPP` report too, with Go's `Aggregation can not be pushed to <store> because <reason>` (`aggregation_push_down_refusals_warn_as_go`; for `approx_count_distinct` Go lists both MPP refusals before the TiKV ones, this port interleaves them). The projection and selection exhausts' TiFlash/TiKV checks (behind Go's `ShouldCheckTiFlashPushDown`) and the MPP join conditions report too (`projection_and_join_push_down_refusals_warn_as_go`). Silent: window frames and the index-merge path builders (`indexmerge_path.go`, `indexmerge_unfinished_path.go`). An EXPLAIN over a scalar subquery shows Go's warnings once where Go shows them twice (Go's subquery scan also shows `stats:partial[...]`).
No lazy InfoSchema V2, schema-cache-size loader/evictor or InfoCache timestamp ranges
BRIE statements are classified but never executed

TopSQL is ported over pprof-rs (`tidb-cpuprofile`, `tidb-topsql-collector`, `tidb-topsql-reporter`, `tidb-topsql`): the status port serves `TopSQLPubSub`, the single-target sink reports to `top-sql.receiver-address`, each command labels its thread `{connID}_{sqlID}`, each statement registers its SQL and plan and labels the thread with both digests, and the profiler's TiDB CPU reaches PROCESSLIST and the statement summary. The DDL worker attaches each job step and each backfill task to the job's SQL (`tidb-ddl` `job_ctx.rs`, Go `ReorgContext.attachTopProfilingInfo`). The step's transaction carries the job's resource-group tagger (`getResourceGroupTaggerForTopSQL`, published into its statement kv context once the step loads the job). Unported: the DXF backfill executor's attach (D02) and the fast-reorg skip checks' (`checkIfTableReorgWorkCanSkip` / `checkIfTempIndexReorgWorkCanSkip`, D02), and the multi-statement prefetch's plan hand-off: `prefetchPointPlanKeys` reads (or locks) the point writes' keys before the statements run (`cluster_session_node/prefetch.rs`, with its `setResourceGroupTaggerForMultiStmtPrefetch`), but its point plans are not handed to the statements (Go `PointPlanKey`), which plan again. Executors register the statement's SQL and plan on their first `Next` with Top profiling on (`RegisterSQLAndPlanInExecForTopProfiling`, `SqlKillerCheckExec`); profiler labels follow Go's goroutine inheritance (`labels::inherit`) into the shuffle, hash-join build, checksum, coprocessor, slow-log parse, cluster-table fan-out, analyze and global-stats merge, DDL analyze workers and the MPP client's store probes

The DDL scheduler, systable manager, history and MDL readers scan records instead of running SQL on `DdlSessionPool::sess_pool`; the bootstrap stages raw rows; accounts load eagerly where Go loads per active user (the site-by-site list is the retired `docs/system-table-sql-execplan.md`, in git at `d64db1f96bc`)

Go's `ExecRestrictedSQL` / `ExecuteInternal` are methods of the issuing session (`withRestrictedSQLExecutor`); this port's executors are adapters beside it (`NodeRestrictedSql`, `SystemSqlExecutor`, `ClusterStatsSqlExecutor`, the plan replayer's `SessionSql`). The node's two apply `ExecOption`'s `SnapshotTS`, `AnalyzeVer`, `AnalyzeSnapshot`, `EnableDDLAnalyze` and `PartitionPruneMode` and restore them as Go's `useCurrentSession` / `getInternalSession` do, but with no issuing session they cannot inherit `OptimizerUseInvisibleIndexes` / `SkipMissingPartitionStats` or append the internal session's warnings to the caller's (`IgnoreWarning`), and `ClusterStatsSqlExecutor` honours the options on the auto-analyze path alone. `rebuildSysVarCache` consumes the rows the domain's sysvar reload loop last read (`SysVarCacheDeps::table_contents`) where Go's runs `fetchTableValues` itself
